      "issue": "perf-budget-and-limits-unset",
      "question": "What latency target, corpus size, result cap and maximum query length should the search meet?",
      "disposition": "escalated",
      "resolution": "The owner must set: a p95 keystroke-to-results latency target, the corpus size to design for, the result cap, and the maximum query length. Components take these as constructor or handler parameters, so the code does not hard-code them. Until the owner sets them, criteria that depend on them cannot be verified. The owner must also confirm that an in-process index is acceptable at the chosen corpus size, because that is the point where the architecture would have to change.",
      "reason": "These numbers are a product commitment and an infrastructure cost judgement. An architect who invents them would have the tests pin values nobody chose.",

      "component": ""
    },
    {

      "question": "Which language and runtime should the project use?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "TypeScript in strict mode on Node.js 20 or later, with npm, vitest, tsc for typecheck and eslint with typescript-eslint for lint. kstrl.toml is absent, so the stack is proposed here for a person to confirm.",
      "reason": "The spec gives no stack, and a typed language with a mature test runner keeps the typecheck and test requirements checkable.",
      "alternative": "Python with pytest and mypy. Rejected only because the browser UI is most naturally written in TypeScript, so one language covers both halves.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "search-architecture-location",
      "question": "Does the index live in the browser or on the server?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "The index is server-side. The browser sends each query to GET /api/search and renders the response.",
      "reason": "Millions of products cannot be shipped to a browser, and the spec asks for millions.",
      "alternative": "A client-side index holding the whole catalog. Rejected because the catalog size makes shipping it to every visitor impractical.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "index-engine-unspecified",
      "question": "Should the search use an external engine or an in-process index?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "An in-process inverted index in the Node process, implemented in catalog-index. The perf-budget-and-limits-unset escalation decides whether this is enough at the stated scale.",
      "reason": "The spec names no infrastructure. Choosing an external engine is an infrastructure commitment for the owner to make, and an in-process index can be replaced behind the same interface later.",
      "alternative": "An external engine such as Elasticsearch, OpenSearch or Postgres full-text search. Rejected because it adds a service the spec does not mention.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "catalog-source-and-shape",
      "question": "Where do products come from and what fields do they have?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "The index is built from a caller-supplied snapshot of { products, brands, categories }. Product is { id, name, brandId?, categoryId? }, Brand is { id, name }, and Category is { id, name }. Loading the snapshot from a data store is a non-goal. The types live in src/search/types.ts.",
      "reason": "A typed snapshot keeps the index testable without a data store, and the shapes are the minimum needed for the three searchable kinds.",
      "alternative": "Read products directly from a database. Rejected because no store is named in the spec.",
      "component": "search-foundation"
    },
    {
      "issue": "match-semantics-unspecified",
      "question": "How does a query match a record?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Each whitespace-separated query token must be a prefix of at least one token in the record's name, brand name or category name. There is no fuzzy or typo matching. Criterion US-003 pins this.",
      "reason": "Token-prefix matching is deterministic, testable and fast on an inverted index. Fuzzy matching is a separate, later feature.",
      "alternative": "Substring matching or fuzzy matching with edit distance. Rejected because substring matching cannot use the index and fuzzy matching adds ranking complexity the spec does not describe.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "ranking-unspecified",
      "question": "In what order are the hits returned?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "Hits whose full normalized name equals the query come first. The rest follow in ascending name order. Criterion US-004 pins this.",
      "reason": "This is the simplest order that puts exact matches first and is deterministic.",
      "alternative": "Score-based relevance with weights per field. Rejected because no weights are specified.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "missing-brand-or-category",
      "question": "How is a product with no brand or category handled?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The product is still indexed and matched by its name. Criterion US-005 pins this.",
      "reason": "Missing optional fields should not hide a product from search.",
      "alternative": "Reject or skip products with missing fields. Rejected because it silently drops catalog items.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "index-update-semantics",
      "question": "Do catalog changes appear immediately or only after a rebuild?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The index is immutable. A catalog change means building a new index from a new snapshot, which then replaces the old one. There are no incremental updates. Criterion US-005 pins this.",
      "reason": "Immutable snapshots are simple to test and avoid locking during reads.",
      "alternative": "Incremental updates to a live index. Rejected because the spec describes no change feed.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "query-normalization-rules",
      "question": "How is query text normalized?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The query is trimmed and lowercased with String.prototype.toLowerCase. Diacritic folding and stemming are not applied. Criterion US-001 pins this.",
      "reason": "This is the smallest rule that makes case-insensitive matching work, and it is testable.",
      "alternative": "Full Unicode folding with NFKD and diacritic removal. Rejected because the spec names no locale requirement.",
      "component": "search-foundation"
    },
    {
      "issue": "endpoint-and-response-shape",
      "question": "What are the API path, the query parameter and the response body?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "GET /api/search?q=<text> returns 200 with JSON { results: Hit[] }, where Hit is { kind: 'product' | 'brand' | 'category', id, label }. The Hit and response types live in src/search/types.ts, so the API and the box share one shape.",
      "reason": "The box and the API must agree on one contract, and the types belong with the shared record types.",
      "alternative": "Separate response types in each component. Rejected because they would drift apart.",
      "component": "search-foundation"
    },
    {
      "issue": "empty-query-behaviour",
      "question": "What does an empty or whitespace-only query return?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "200 with { results: [] } and no index call. Criterion US-007 pins this.",
      "reason": "An empty query is a valid state while the user is typing, so it should not be an error.",
      "alternative": "400 for an empty query. Rejected because it would make every cleared search box look like an error.",
      "component": "search-api"
    },
    {
      "issue": "invalid-request-behaviour",
      "question": "How are malformed requests answered?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "A missing q returns 400 with a JSON error. A q longer than the maximum query length returns 400. A non-GET method returns 405. Criteria US-006 and US-007 pin this.",
      "reason": "These are the standard HTTP responses for these cases.",
      "alternative": "Silently treat a missing q as empty. Rejected because it hides client bugs.",
      "component": "search-api"
    },
    {
      "issue": "authentication-and-access",
      "question": "Does search require authentication?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Search is a public, read-only endpoint with no authentication or authorization. Per-user results and personalization are non-goals.",
      "reason": "The spec describes a storefront search box with no accounts or roles.",
      "alternative": "Authenticated search. Rejected because the spec names no users or accounts.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "abuse-and-rate-limiting",
      "question": "How is abusive request volume handled on a public endpoint?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Rate limiting is out of scope for this run and is recorded as a non-goal. The deployment owner must add rate limiting at the edge before going live. This is a risk acceptance for this run, and the owner should confirm it.",
      "reason": "Rate limiting depends on the deployment topology, which the spec does not describe, so it cannot be implemented correctly in the component.",
      "alternative": "Add an in-process rate limiter. Rejected because it would be ineffective across several server instances.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "host-page-and-mounting",
      "question": "Where is the search box placed and how is it mounted?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "search-box-ui exports mountSearchBox(container: HTMLElement, options?: { fetch?: typeof fetch }). Placing it on a host page, and starting the HTTP server, are non-goals.",
      "reason": "A mount function is testable with jsdom and leaves page placement to the owner.",
      "alternative": "A full page with routing. Rejected because the spec describes only a search box.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "realtime-definition",
      "question": "Does 'real time' mean a request per keystroke or a debounced request?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "A request is sent for each input change, with no debounce, and any request still in flight is aborted. Criterion US-008 pins this.",
      "reason": "This needs no interval value that the spec does not state, and the latency question is left to the escalation.",
      "alternative": "Debounce by a fixed interval. Rejected because the interval is unstated.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "stale-response-handling",
      "question": "What happens when an older response arrives after a newer request?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "Each request carries a sequence number. A response for any request that is no longer the latest is discarded without rendering. Criterion US-008 pins this.",
      "reason": "Without this rule the box can show results for a query the user has already changed.",
      "alternative": "Render every response as it arrives. Rejected because results could go out of order.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "network-error-ui",
      "question": "What does the box show when the request fails?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "A network error or non-2xx response shows an error message in the status element. The input stays enabled. Criterion US-009 pins this.",
      "reason": "A failed search should be visible to the user without blocking further input.",
      "alternative": "Clear the results silently. Rejected because the user cannot tell a failure from an empty result.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "empty-results-message",
      "question": "What does the box show when nothing matches?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The status element shows the text 'No results'. Criterion US-009 pins this.",
      "reason": "A visible no-results state is needed to tell an empty result from a loading one.",
      "alternative": "Show nothing. Rejected because the user cannot tell whether the search ran.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "accessibility-unspecified",
      "question": "What accessibility behavior does the box have?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The input has an accessible label, and result changes are announced through a status element with role status. Criterion US-009 pins this.",
      "reason": "A live-updating control must announce its results to screen reader users.",
      "alternative": "No accessibility behavior. Rejected because it would exclude assistive-technology users.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "modern-best-practices-undefined",
      "question": "Which practices count as modern best practices?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Strict TypeScript; native fetch with AbortController; no UI framework; automated tests with vitest; one lockfile committed; lint and typecheck gates.",
      "reason": "These practices can each be checked, and the spec gives no other measurable meaning.",
      "alternative": "A framework such as React. Rejected because the spec asks for one search box and names no framework.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "lint-check-unspecified",
      "question": "Should lint be a gate?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Yes. The lint check is npm run lint, running eslint with typescript-eslint, and every change must pass it.",
      "reason": "Lint gates keep the code consistent, and the cost is small.",
      "alternative": "Tests and typecheck only, as the spec states. Rejected because the spec's list is not a complete set of gates.",
      "component": ""

{
  "stack": {
    "instructions": "TypeScript with strict mode on Node.js 20 or later, managed with npm. Dependencies are declared in package.json and locked in package-lock.json, which search-foundation creates and which must be committed. Source lives in src/, tests in tests/ (vitest). UI tests opt into jsdom with a per-file @vitest-environment comment. Use native fetch and AbortController, with no UI framework. Search runs server-side against an in-process inverted index. Run every check from the repository root.",
    "setup": "",
    "env": [],
    "checks": {

  "spec_issues": [
    {

    {
      "id": "search-architecture-location",

    {

    {
      "id": "missing-brand-or-category",

    {
      "id": "abuse-and-rate-limiting",
      "severity": "major",
      "kind": "undefined_failure_mode",

    {
      "id": "host-page-and-mounting",

      "summary": "The spec does not say where the search box is placed or how a page mounts it.",

      "location": "Requirements: 'Show results in real time'",
      "suggestion": "Define a request per input change, with no debounce, and cancel the request still in flight."
    },
    {
      "id": "stale-response-handling",
      "severity": "major",
      "kind": "undefined_failure_mode",
      "summary": "The spec does not say what happens when an older response arrives after a newer request.",
      "location": "Requirements: 'Show results in real time'",
      "suggestion": "Discard any response that is not for the latest request."
    },
    {
      "id": "network-error-ui",
      "severity": "major",
      "kind": "undefined_failure_mode",
      "summary": "The spec does not say how the box behaves when the search request fails.",
      "location": "Requirements: 'Show results in real time'",
      "suggestion": "Show an error message in the status element and keep the input usable."
    },
    {
      "id": "empty-results-message",
      "severity": "minor",

      "location": "Requirements: 'Show results in real time'",
      "suggestion": "Show a no-results message in the status element."
    },
    {
      "id": "accessibility-unspecified",
      "severity": "minor",
      "kind": "missing_detail",
      "summary": "The spec states no accessibility requirement for a live-updating search control.",
      "location": "Requirements: 'Build a search box'",
      "suggestion": "Give the input an accessible name and announce result changes through a status region."
    },
    {
      "id": "modern-best-practices-undefined",
      "severity": "minor",
      "kind": "ambiguity",
      "summary": "'Use modern best practices' does not name any practice an engineer must follow.",
      "location": "Requirements: 'Use modern best practices'",
      "suggestion": "Name the concrete practices: strict TypeScript, native fetch with AbortController, and automated tests."
    },
    {
      "id": "lint-check-unspecified",
      "severity": "minor",
      "kind": "other",
      "summary": "The spec's closing line lists only tests and typecheck, and says nothing about lint.",
      "location": "'Tests pass. Typecheck passes.'",
      "suggestion": "Add a lint check so that every change is linted."
    }
  ],
  "decisions": [
    {
      "issue": "perf-budget-and-limits-unset",
      "question": "What latency target, corpus size, result cap and maximum query length should the search meet?",
      "disposition": "escalated",
      "resolution": "The owner must set: a p95 keystroke-to-results latency target, the corpus size to design for, the result cap, and the maximum query length. Components take these as constructor or handler parameters, so the code does not hard-code them. Until the owner sets them, criteria that depend on them cannot be verified. The owner must also confirm that an in-process index is acceptable at the chosen corpus size, because that is the point where the architecture would have to change.",
      "reason": "These numbers are a product commitment and an infrastructure cost judgement. An architect who invents them would have the tests pin values nobody chose.",
      "alternative": "Assume a latency target and a corpus size, and write them into acceptance criteria. Rejected because the values would be invented.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "tech-stack-unspecified",
      "question": "Which language and runtime should the project use?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "TypeScript in strict mode on Node.js 20 or later, with npm, vitest, tsc for typecheck and eslint with typescript-eslint for lint. kstrl.toml is absent, so the stack is proposed here for a person to confirm.",
      "reason": "The spec gives no stack, and a typed language with a mature test runner keeps the typecheck and test requirements checkable.",
      "alternative": "Python with pytest and mypy. Rejected only because the browser UI is most naturally written in TypeScript, so one language covers both halves.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "search-architecture-location",
      "question": "Does the index live in the browser or on the server?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "The index is server-side. The browser sends each query to GET /api/search and renders the response.",
      "reason": "Millions of products cannot be shipped to a browser, and the spec asks for millions.",
      "alternative": "A client-side index holding the whole catalog. Rejected because the catalog size makes shipping it to every visitor impractical.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "index-engine-unspecified",
      "question": "Should the search use an external engine or an in-process index?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "An in-process inverted index in the Node process, implemented in catalog-index. The perf-budget-and-limits-unset escalation decides whether this is enough at the stated scale.",
      "reason": "The spec names no infrastructure. Choosing an external engine is an infrastructure commitment for the owner to make, and an in-process index can be replaced behind the same interface later.",
      "alternative": "An external engine such as Elasticsearch, OpenSearch or Postgres full-text search. Rejected because it adds a service the spec does not mention.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "catalog-source-and-shape",
      "question": "Where do products come from and what fields do they have?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "The index is built from a caller-supplied snapshot of { products, brands, categories }. Product is { id, name, brandId?, categoryId? }, Brand is { id, name }, and Category is { id, name }. Loading the snapshot from a data store is a non-goal. The types live in src/search/types.ts.",
      "reason": "A typed snapshot keeps the index testable without a data store, and the shapes are the minimum needed for the three searchable kinds.",
      "alternative": "Read products directly from a database. Rejected because no store is named in the spec.",
      "component": "search-foundation"
    },
    {
      "issue": "match-semantics-unspecified",
      "question": "How does a query match a record?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Each whitespace-separated query token must be a prefix of at least one token in the record's name, brand name or category name. There is no fuzzy or typo matching. Criterion US-003 pins this.",
      "reason": "Token-prefix matching is deterministic, testable and fast on an inverted index. Fuzzy matching is a separate, later feature.",
      "alternative": "Substring matching or fuzzy matching with edit distance. Rejected because substring matching cannot use the index and fuzzy matching adds ranking complexity the spec does not describe.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "ranking-unspecified",
      "question": "In what order are the hits returned?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "Hits whose full normalized name equals the query come first. The rest follow in ascending name order. Criterion US-004 pins this.",
      "reason": "This is the simplest order that puts exact matches first and is deterministic.",
      "alternative": "Score-based relevance with weights per field. Rejected because no weights are specified.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "missing-brand-or-category",
      "question": "How is a product with no brand or category handled?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The product is still indexed and matched by its name. Criterion US-005 pins this.",
      "reason": "Missing optional fields should not hide a product from search.",
      "alternative": "Reject or skip products with missing fields. Rejected because it silently drops catalog items.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "index-update-semantics",
      "question": "Do catalog changes appear immediately or only after a rebuild?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The index is immutable. A catalog change means building a new index from a new snapshot, which then replaces the old one. There are no incremental updates. Criterion US-005 pins this.",
      "reason": "Immutable snapshots are simple to test and avoid locking during reads.",
      "alternative": "Incremental updates to a live index. Rejected because the spec describes no change feed.",
      "component": "catalog-index"
    },
    {
      "issue": "query-normalization-rules",
      "question": "How is query text normalized?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The query is trimmed and lowercased with String.prototype.toLowerCase. Diacritic folding and stemming are not applied. Criterion US-001 pins this.",
      "reason": "This is the smallest rule that makes case-insensitive matching work, and it is testable.",
      "alternative": "Full Unicode folding with NFKD and diacritic removal. Rejected because the spec names no locale requirement.",
      "component": "search-foundation"
    },
    {
      "issue": "endpoint-and-response-shape",
      "question": "What are the API path, the query parameter and the response body?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "GET /api/search?q=<text> returns 200 with JSON { results: Hit[] }, where Hit is { kind: 'product' | 'brand' | 'category', id, label }. The Hit and response types live in src/search/types.ts, so the API and the box share one shape.",
      "reason": "The box and the API must agree on one contract, and the types belong with the shared record types.",
      "alternative": "Separate response types in each component. Rejected because they would drift apart.",
      "component": "search-foundation"
    },
    {
      "issue": "empty-query-behaviour",
      "question": "What does an empty or whitespace-only query return?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "200 with { results: [] } and no index call. Criterion US-007 pins this.",
      "reason": "An empty query is a valid state while the user is typing, so it should not be an error.",
      "alternative": "400 for an empty query. Rejected because it would make every cleared search box look like an error.",
      "component": "search-api"
    },
    {
      "issue": "invalid-request-behaviour",
      "question": "How are malformed requests answered?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "A missing q returns 400 with a JSON error. A q longer than the maximum query length returns 400. A non-GET method returns 405. Criteria US-006 and US-007 pin this.",
      "reason": "These are the standard HTTP responses for these cases.",
      "alternative": "Silently treat a missing q as empty. Rejected because it hides client bugs.",
      "component": "search-api"
    },
    {
      "issue": "authentication-and-access",
      "question": "Does search require authentication?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Search is a public, read-only endpoint with no authentication or authorization. Per-user results and personalization are non-goals.",
      "reason": "The spec describes a storefront search box with no accounts or roles.",
      "alternative": "Authenticated search. Rejected because the spec names no users or accounts.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "abuse-and-rate-limiting",
      "question": "How is abusive request volume handled on a public endpoint?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Rate limiting is out of scope for this run and is recorded as a non-goal. The deployment owner must add rate limiting at the edge before going live. This is a risk acceptance for this run, and the owner should confirm it.",
      "reason": "Rate limiting depends on the deployment topology, which the spec does not describe, so it cannot be implemented correctly in the component.",
      "alternative": "Add an in-process rate limiter. Rejected because it would be ineffective across several server instances.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "host-page-and-mounting",
      "question": "Where is the search box placed and how is it mounted?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "search-box-ui exports mountSearchBox(container: HTMLElement, options?: { fetch?: typeof fetch }). Placing it on a host page, and starting the HTTP server, are non-goals.",
      "reason": "A mount function is testable with jsdom and leaves page placement to the owner.",
      "alternative": "A full page with routing. Rejected because the spec describes only a search box.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "realtime-definition",
      "question": "Does 'real time' mean a request per keystroke or a debounced request?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "A request is sent for each input change, with no debounce, and any request still in flight is aborted. Criterion US-008 pins this.",
      "reason": "This needs no interval value that the spec does not state, and the latency question is left to the escalation.",
      "alternative": "Debounce by a fixed interval. Rejected because the interval is unstated.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "stale-response-handling",
      "question": "What happens when an older response arrives after a newer request?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "Each request carries a sequence number. A response for any request that is no longer the latest is discarded without rendering. Criterion US-008 pins this.",
      "reason": "Without this rule the box can show results for a query the user has already changed.",
      "alternative": "Render every response as it arrives. Rejected because results could go out of order.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "network-error-ui",
      "question": "What does the box show when the request fails?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "A network error or non-2xx response shows an error message in the status element. The input stays enabled. Criterion US-009 pins this.",
      "reason": "A failed search should be visible to the user without blocking further input.",
      "alternative": "Clear the results silently. Rejected because the user cannot tell a failure from an empty result.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "empty-results-message",
      "question": "What does the box show when nothing matches?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The status element shows the text 'No results'. Criterion US-009 pins this.",
      "reason": "A visible no-results state is needed to tell an empty result from a loading one.",
      "alternative": "Show nothing. Rejected because the user cannot tell whether the search ran.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "accessibility-unspecified",
      "question": "What accessibility behavior does the box have?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The input has an accessible label, and result changes are announced through a status element with role status. Criterion US-009 pins this.",
      "reason": "A live-updating control must announce its results to screen reader users.",
      "alternative": "No accessibility behavior. Rejected because it would exclude assistive-technology users.",
      "component": "search-box-ui"
    },
    {
      "issue": "modern-best-practices-undefined",
      "question": "Which practices count as modern best practices?",
      "disposition": "decided",
